clue.text: Choose to keep quiet time in smoker's assembly

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it within, so the word for choose wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: to choose is to pick
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone opts to hold a silent moment amid a gathering of smokers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Choose to keep quiet' reads as a call for silence, but 'to keep' is the container signal, and the definition is the closing phrase about a smoker.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand for holding tobacco pipes is a fitting piece of furniture for a pipe smoker, here jokingly called an assembly.

clue.text: Don't go to the Pays Bas without a translator

indicators.note: a translator turns words into new form, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: French for the Netherlands, taken as letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice to skip the Netherlands if you have no interpreter.
explanation.walkthrough: Without one A, the letters of PAYS BAS rearrange ('translator') to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To go past a place without stopping means not going to it.

clue.text: Proper way to specify delegated correspondent

indicators.note: way suggests a different manner or arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: The correct method for naming a stand-in letter-writer.
explanation.walkthrough: Short for per procurationem, written before a signature when signing on someone else's behalf.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin abbreviation marks a letter signed by an agent for the sender, naming delegated correspondence.

clue.text: On holiday the setter's been far from dominant

parts.note: a recess is a break or holiday, as in Parliament
the setter speaking is 'I', and I have been is I've

explanation.surface: Away on a break, the compiler has been nowhere near the top.
explanation.definitionFit: In genetics a trait that is masked by a stronger gene is the opposite of dominant.

clue.text: Bird is captured — where? — in Italy

parts.note: collared means caught or captured
dove is Italian for where, signalled by 'in Italy'

explanation.surface: A bird has been seized, and someone asks where in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: A type of dove common in Europe, named for the black ring at its neck.

clue.text: Sailor to accomplish his aim

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor
to get something done is to accomplish it

explanation.surface: A seaman sets out to achieve his ambition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: what one aims at is the object one is trying to hit or reach.

clue.text: A place for such as 4 in the rigging

parts.note: doves and pigeons are kept in a loft

explanation.surface: A roost for doves high among a ship's ropes.
explanation.definitionFit: Up high, as in a ship's rigging, is the meaning of this adverb.

clue.text: See 19
Learned work on pacts needing little change

indicators.note: a small change of position for one letter turns the word for pacts into the answer

parts.note: treaties are pacts

explanation.surface: A scholarly book about agreements that barely need revising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing little change' moves the S of TREATIES one place earlier.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal scholarly essay is a learned work.

clue.text: Programme of talent-spotting, being rubbish?

parts.note: 'talent' is slang for attractive women ('...'), and the closing idiom means worthless

explanation.surface: A grumble that a TV talent show is trash.
explanation.walkthrough: Strictly Come Dancing is a BBC dance-contest show, often just called Strictly; the idiom 'for the birds' means worthless.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase combines the show's nickname with an American idiom meaning trivial or worthless, matching 'being rubbish'.

clue.text: See 9
Barker puts pile of stones on land register

parts.note: a cairn is a heap of stones marking a spot
a terrier is an old word for a register of landed property

explanation.surface: A dog puts a heap of rocks on the property records.
explanation.definitionFit: A small Scottish terrier breed is a dog, and dogs bark.

clue.text: See 9
Painters etc in suitable accommodation

indicators.note: the painters are placed in the word for suitable

parts.note: apt means suitable
painters and other artists are art men

explanation.surface: Decorators at work in a fitting place to live.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat or set of rooms is a type of accommodation.

clue.text: Celebratory explosive devices put in sack — barmy!

parts.note: to sack someone is to fire them
barmy and crackers both mean mad

explanation.surface: Fireworks shoved in a bag: a crazy idea!
explanation.definitionFit: Small bangers set off at festivities are explosive devices used for celebration.

clue.text: American playwright about to receive into the Church of England a French one

indicators.note: into puts the playwright inside the letters for the Church

parts.note: CE abbreviates Church of England

indicators.note: about means the playwright goes round the next letter

parts.note: Eugene O'Neill was an American dramatist
R is an abbreviation for receive

explanation.surface: A US dramatist is about to be welcomed into the Anglican church by a Frenchman.
explanation.walkthrough: R for 'receive' is a dictionary abbreviation. 'about' signals the playwright's name wrapping that letter, and 'into' sends the result inside the Church's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierre Corneille was a seventeenth-century French tragedian, so a French playwright.

clue.text: Jewellery and stuff, including English food

parts.note: ice is slang for diamonds

indicators.note: the word for stuff includes the letter for English

parts.note: to cram is to stuff

explanation.surface: Gems and goods, plus some English cuisine.
explanation.definitionFit: A frozen dessert is a kind of food.

clue.text: Dominant monkey to get large gin cocktail

parts.note: a cheeky child is an imp or a monkey
OS is outsize, large

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters of gin are mixed

explanation.surface: A mischievous creature gets a big mixed drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Commanding or grand in appearance, close to dominant.

clue.text: In the centre, order to repair a model of the statue that came to dinner

definitions.text: the statue that came to dinner

indicators.note: the following pieces are placed in the word for the centre

parts.note: the core is the centre
OM is the Order of Merit
to mend is to repair
the Model T was Ford's famous car

explanation.surface: Instructions in the middle to fix a model of a statue that dined with someone.
explanation.walkthrough: In Mozart's Don Giovanni, the statue of the murdered Commendatore accepts the Don's dinner invitation and drags him to hell.
explanation.definitionFit: Mozart's opera gives the murdered knight-commander's statue, which comes to supper, this title as its name.

clue.text: Watch American gun being used in Britain by king that's no agriculturalist

parts.note: a hunter is a pocket watch with a hinged cover
gat is American slang for a gun
a British setter is here
R is rex, king

explanation.surface: A timepiece and a US firearm used in the UK by a monarch who doesn't farm.
explanation.definitionFit: Early humans who foraged and hunted rather than farmed are defined in contrast to agriculturalists.

clue.text: Optimistic — don't come in yet!

definitions.meaning: in music, the unstressed beat before a bar, so a player waits for it before coming in

explanation.definitionFit: Cheerful and hopeful; in music also the weak beat before the downbeat.

clue.text: Annoyed about combining styles?

parts.note: cross means annoyed
over can mean about, concerning

explanation.surface: Irritated by a mixing of genres.
explanation.definitionFit: A work that blends genres, such as music mixing pop and classical, is called by this term.

clue.text: Satirist, one of the 12

explanation.definitionFit: Jonathan Swift was an Irish satirist, and swifts are fast-flying birds.

clue.text: Provide joke with point

parts.note: E is east, a compass point
a quip is a joke

explanation.surface: Supply a gag that has a punchline.
explanation.definitionFit: To kit out or furnish someone is to provide them with what they need.

clue.text: Priest turned farceur sought by alchemist

parts.note: Eli is the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible

indicators.note: turned means the farceur's name is read backwards

parts.note: Brian Rix was a British actor famous for stage farces

explanation.surface: A clergyman turned comedian is wanted by a medieval chemist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses RIX to give XIR. Brian Rix led the Whitehall farces in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Alchemists searched for a potion of eternal life alongside the philosopher's stone.

clue.text: Person from Riga in unpleasant surroundings — is it Brussels?

indicators.note: the person from Riga sits in the unpleasant surroundings

parts.note: vile means unpleasant, here forming the outside
a Lett is a Latvian, and Riga is Latvia's capital

explanation.surface: A Latvian stuck somewhere nasty wonders if it's the Belgian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Charlotte Brontë's novel Villette is set in a fictional town modelled on Brussels.
explanation.definitionFit: The novel's fictional city stands for Brussels, so the question names it by its real model.

clue.text: Strong possibility that you could start?

parts.note: might expresses possibility, as in 'it might rain'

indicators.note: start means the first letter of the word you

explanation.surface: A good chance that you could get going?
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: powerful or very strong.

clue.text: Time Rugby Union's Tiger played with genuine resolution

indicators.note: played suggests the letters of Tiger are moved about

explanation.surface: A rugby player nicknamed Tiger performed with real determination.
explanation.definitionFit: True means genuine and grit means resolution or pluck; the phrase is also a famous Western.
